newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Pacer sees higher Q3 net.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Pacer sees higher Q3 net.

text.p: Pacer Technology Inc expects net income for the third quarter to grow about 25 percent from the comparable year-ago quarter, Pacer President and Chief Executive Officer James Munn said.

Pacer expects sales for the third quarter, ended March 31, to be about $6.6 million up from $5.5 million in the year-ago period. The company expects net income of about $350,000, or $0.02 a share, up from $281,628, or $0.02 a share in the year-ago quarter.

"We are a little bit ahead of our (growth) targets," Munn said in an interview. "We set our targets at the beginning of the year and we were pretty agressive with it and we really have exceeded our expectations."

For the nine-months Pacer sees sales of about $19 million up from $16.5 million in the year-ago period. The company expects net income of about $835,000, or $0.05 a share, up from $635,587, or $0.04 a share, in 1996.
Pacer is expected to report its results later this week.
Operating income for the quarter is expected to be 48 percent higher than the year-ago quarter and 64 percent higher for the nine months.
Fuelling those higher margins were economies of scale enjoyed from higher sales as well as upgrades to the company's manufacturing machinery, Munn said.

In 1978 when Pacer went public, it made super glue for the hobby market of boats, cars and airplanes. Since the current management team joined the company in 1986 it has expanded into adhesives for electronics, aerospace, automotive sealants, cosmetic nailcare products as well as private-label products for other companies. Since then the company has expanded its international sales base to 70 countries.

Pacer entered the retail business in 1993 through its acquisition of Super Glue Corp taking it into almost every mass merchandiser in the United States including grocery chains, drug stores and hardware stores.
Munn said he sees the company's growth continuing.
"Average growth for the next five years, which will include acquisitions ..., we think we will grow between 20 percent and 25 percent per year," Munn said.
That sort of growth, if achieved, would put annual sales at between $50 million and $60 million in five years.
"We think we are undervalued in our stock price ... we think people should take a position in our stock," said Munn who is on a roadshow aimed at attacting investors to the stock.
Munn said Pacer is interested in buying the type of company that has complimentary products but is struggling because it is lacking the sort of distribution that Pacer has.
"We can take those products and basically in a very short period of time have them in maybe 10,000 outlets," Munn said. "We are looking at (acquisitions) from $2 million to $50 million."
